html:
The Casbah is the old city of Algiers, a maze of white houses, narrow lanes and mosques climbing the hill above the port. Most of it was built in the time of the Ottoman Regency, from the 1500s, on the site of a much older town.

At the top stands the citadel, the last palace of the deys. Below lay the homes of corsair captains, merchants and craftsmen, built around inner courtyards. The French cut wide streets through its lower part after 1830.

In 1956 and 1957 the Casbah was the base of the FLN fighters in the battle for Algiers, shown in the film The Battle of Algiers. It became a World Heritage Site in 1992, but many houses are crumbling. See also Barbarossa.
